limits: Triage only. The model ranks findings by how much they look like past candidates that survived triage. It does not verify anything.
Zero verified-real positives exist in the training data, so the model never predicts VERIFIED_REAL and must never be used to claim one. A high score means 'worth a live probe', nothing more.

Label skew: the training set is 85% worth-validating / 15% likely-false-positive (2249 positive / 398 negative of 2647 rows). Accuracy near the majority baseline means the model learned nothing; judge it by minority-class recall and ROC AUC instead.
Findings from plugins or chains unseen in training fall into the OTHER bucket; the model has no opinion about them beyond the generic features.

Bayesian: the score is a posterior MEAN with a 90% credible interval; findings whose interval straddles 0.5 are flagged unsure (nn_unsure) and routed to human review instead of auto-triage. The interval is calibrated on the training split only; test coverage is reported, not assumed.

bayesian.method: last-layer Laplace approximation over the trained MAP MLP (see backend/docs/nn-bayesian.md)

calibration.note: scale fitted on TRAIN only; test coverage is reported separately and will differ
